en: The Apadāna of the Elder Ucchukhaṇḍika Ekavihārivagga 5 The Apadāna of the Elder Ucchukhaṇḍika: When I was a sugar-cane cutter in the city of Benares, I offered a stalk of sugar-cane to the Buddha Vipassī. Because of that root of merit, I have never experienced suffering; For twenty thousand aeons, I dwelt in the realm of the gods. Having passed away from there, I was reborn in the human world, And I attained the fruit of stream-entry, free from doubt. Through this very same deed, I have now reached the final body; Having abandoned all defilements, I have attained parinibbāna. Thus did the Elder Ucchukhaṇḍika speak of his own past deeds.
“In the city of Bandhumatī,
I was a gatekeeper;
there I saw the stainless Buddha.”
To the one who has gone beyond all phenomena,
I gave a piece of sugarcane to the Best of Buddhas.
With a clear mind and joyful heart,
[I offered it] to Vipassi, the Great Seer,
ninety-one aeons ago.
Since I gave that sugarcane at that time,
I have not known a miserable rebirth;
this is the fruit of that piece of sugarcane.
The defilements have been burnt away by me;
I dwell free from taints.
Welcome indeed has come to me...
[as before] ...the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
The four analytical knowledges...
[and so on] ...the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Uccukhaṇḍika spoke these verses.
This is the fifth legend of the elder Uccukhaṇḍika.
